analysis.title: Weekly Markets Monitor, 23 November 2026: A(I) reckoning
key_insights: Gold fell 8.9% to Friday's New York close as AI and tech valuation concerns triggered broad de-leveraging. Gold was hit as a liquid asset during risk reduction.
Equities sold off on AI concerns. Nvidia slumped despite strong earnings after reports of an SEC accounting probe, and Anthropic's record IPO gave back much of its debut gains.
Fed minutes showed almost all officials expect to hike in December, and larger hikes could be needed. Implied peak Fed Funds fell from 4.7% on 13 November to 4.5% on Friday.
Gold ETF outflows in November were led by Europe (-16t), while North America led last week (-12t). Outflows from sticky ETFs were modest.
COMEX managed money, other reportables and non-reportables fell a combined 75t by 17 November, and open interest fell another 35t by Friday. SHFE net positioning fell 11t, which was not dramatic.
25-delta risk reversals fell across 1m, 3m and 6m, signalling more demand for downside protection, but the moves look orderly.

WGC sees risks to gold roughly balanced near term. A bounce is possible given stretched commodity positioning, but a positioning washout has not yet occurred. Risks include further AI stock rout, rotation into bonds, hawkish Fed minutes and an upside PCE surprise Wednesday.

Technicals: gold broke Fibonacci support at $3,858 and is testing $3,500, a 37% fall from the January peak. A break targets $3,450/3,439 then $3,320 and $3,305 (200dma-based floor). Resistance at $3,595 and $3,835/3,870.

The USD (BBDXY) broke above 1229/1233 resistance, which WGC reads as completion of a major base and a headwind for gold. Next resistance is 1249 then 1261, and a drop below 1217 would neutralise the base.
10yr US real yields fell after being capped below the 2.975% YTD high, with support at 2.72/2.71% and 2.68%. WGC views the pullback as temporary within a larger triangle continuation pattern.

Nasdaq 100 is 20% below its peak, in bear market territory, and the S&P 500 is over 10% below its October peak. The S&P is holding 6900 support, with 6817 and 6695 next. MSCI ACWI broke its 200-day average, with support at 1016 then 995/958.
Gold options show elevated vol: GLD 1M IV 31.99 at the 90.3 percentile of its 1Y range, 30D realized vol 28.25.
Macro recap: Eurozone October CPI 4.0% y/y, China October industrial production 4.8% y/y, Japan Q3 GDP -0.1% annualised, US retail sales +0.2% m/m. Week ahead centres on October PCE on Wednesday.
Bitcoin fell 13.75% W/W to 58,930, and silver fell 15.56% W/W to 41.2.

tension_points.bear_case: The USD has completed a major base, positioning has not fully washed out, and hawkish Fed minutes plus a possible upside PCE could add pressure.
